newsitem.title: USA: US Postal Service limits packages for UPS strike.
newsitem.headline: US Postal Service limits packages for UPS strike.

text.p: The U.S. Postal Service said on Monday that it will limit the number of parcels customers can mail at a single time and take other steps to handle an expected increase in volume in light of the UPS strike.
Customers bringing parcels to a post office will be limited to four packages each visit.
People with five or more parcel post items or priority mail parcels will be required to make appointments at specific parcel drop facilities in their area, the Postal Service said.
However, customers using first class mail, priority MAil letters and flats will not be affected and no new restrictions will be placed on express mail.
The new measures are effective immediately. The Postal Service said in a statement that these were "short-term measures designed to help manage a short-term situation."
"Naturally, the Postal Service would like to have this increased parcel post business over the long term," Postmaster General Marvin Runyon said in a statement.
The Postal Service handles less than 10 percent of the parcel market, while UPS holds more than 80 percent and delivers about 12 million pieces a day, the Postal Service said.
